engine.title: Stop buying strength that has already run
engine.body: The 4H RSI ceiling for longs was 75. Splitting every closed trade by the RSI recorded at entry showed the engine bleeding above 65 and profitable below it. The ceiling is now 65.
engine.note: Holds in both halves of the sample and at every cut point tested (60, 65, 70), so it is not one lucky threshold. The threshold was still chosen from this sample, so treat the size as an upper bound.

engine.title: A break-even stop would not have helped
engine.body: The median losing trade was +1.44R in profit before it reversed, and 59% touched a full +1R first. That looks like an obvious fix: move the stop to entry once price pays 1R. Re-walking every trade bar by bar, with winners subject to the same rule, says otherwise.
engine.note: The first version of this test only altered losers, which guarantees a positive answer. Correcting it reversed the conclusion. Nothing tested cleared one standard error, so no stop rule was adopted.

engine.title: Trades were being closed at prices that never traded
engine.body: The grader had never resolved a single trade — an exception was being swallowed silently — leaving a fallback path that could book an exit at a bar from before the signal existed. Every closed trade was re-graded against bars that actually printed.
evidence: exits corrected to a real price
engine.note: This moved the headline number against me. It is published anyway, because the earlier number was not real. Pre-correction data is kept in the repo rather than deleted.

engine.title: A first target must pay back the risk
engine.body: T1 was whichever structural level sat nearest the entry, with no distance test. One signal shipped a T1 worth 0.19R against its own stop, printed beside an R:R of 2.41 quoted off T2. T1 must now return at least 1R.

chess.title: Rating Progress Reality
chess.body: 800→1000: Learn not to blunder pieces for free. 1000→1200: Basic tactics (forks, pins). 1200→1500: Strategy (plans, pawn structure). 1500→1800: Calculation depth + endgames. 1800+: Opening theory + deep calculation. Most adults plateau at 1000-1200 because they skip tactics training. Do 10 puzzles daily — minimum. No shortcut.

wisdom.title: The Long Game of Parenting
wisdom.body: You won't remember 2026 as a year. You'll remember it as the year your daughter started talking, your first steps in Dubai, the grind that changed everything. Keep a journal. Even one line per day. In 10 years, you'll read it and understand why it was worth it.

book.author: Nassim Taleb
book.chapter: Build Systems That Gain From Disorder
book.lesson: Taleb's central idea: the opposite of fragile is not robust (survives shocks unchanged) — it is antifragile (gets stronger from shocks). Your muscles are antifragile — stress them and they grow. Your immune system is antifragile. Most institutions are fragile — they optimise for efficiency and have no slack, so unexpected shocks destroy them. To build antifragility: have optionality (many small bets, not one big one), avoid debt (debt makes you fragile to cash flow shocks), benefit from volatility (career skills that are more valuable in crisis than in calm), and build redundancy (slack is not waste — it's the shock absorber).
book.key_quote: Don't just plan to survive crises. Build a life and career that becomes stronger because of them.
book.action: Identify one area of your life (financial, professional, health) that is fragile — one shock away from breaking. What would make it antifragile?
crux: Three categories: fragile (breaks under stress), robust (resists), antifragile (improves).
The opposite of fragile is not robust. It is antifragile — gaining from disorder.
Absence of evidence of fragility is not evidence of robustness. Turkeys learn this at Thanksgiving.
Via negativa: improvement comes more reliably from removal than addition.
Barbell strategy: extreme safety on most of the exposure, extreme risk on a small slice. Never the middle.
Optionality lets you gain from uncertainty without needing to forecast it.
Hormesis: small doses of stress strengthen. Zero stress atrophies.
Naive intervention causes iatrogenic harm — the cure does the damage. Doing nothing is often correct.
Skin in the game is the only real filter. Ignore forecasts from people who bear no cost for being wrong.
Fragility is measurable and predictable; future events are not. Measure the exposure, not the odds.
Time is the best test of durability. The Lindy effect: what has survived long tends to keep surviving.
Redundancy looks inefficient and is actually insurance. Nature runs two kidneys.
Small and decentralised is antifragile; large and centralised is fragile.
Touristification — removing all volatility — makes systems and people brittle.
learnings: Optimise for surviving the worst case, not for the expected case.
Removing the bad reliably beats adding the good.
Anyone forecasting without downside exposure should be discounted to zero.
Efficiency and fragility are usually the same thing wearing different clothes.
examples: Restaurants are individually fragile and the restaurant sector is antifragile — constant failure improves the survivors.
The 2008 banking system was optimised for efficiency, held minimal buffers, and broke. Small distributed lenders did not.
Taleb's barbell in practice: 90% in treasuries, 10% in far out-of-the-money options. Capped loss, uncapped gain.
adapt: Barbell the income: stable FP&A salary as the safe leg, Codex and trading as the small convex leg. No middle-risk bets.
Multiple income paths beat one optimised one. Meta restriction proved single-channel dependence is fragile.
Via negativa on the product: deleting /fno, /options, /portfolio improved TradeFlow. Removal was the upgrade.
Redundancy on the bots: Railway shut down and took the command handler with it. One host is one point of failure.

minimalism.title: Gifts Are Not Obligations
minimalism.body: A gift's job ended the moment it was given. Keeping something unwanted out of guilt honours nobody and costs you space every day.
minimalism.action: Release one guilt-kept item. The giver will never know.
minimalism.label: Minimalism

etiquette.title: Do Not Correct Trivia In Public
etiquette.body: Being right about something small in front of an audience costs more in goodwill than the correction is worth. Let it go, or say it privately later.
etiquette.action: Let one minor inaccuracy pass uncorrected today.
etiquette.label: Etiquette

stillness.title: Impermanence Applies To The Bad Too
stillness.body: The difficult period ends. So does the good one. This is not pessimism — it is the only reliable source of equanimity in both directions.
stillness.action: Name the current difficulty. Say plainly: this also ends.
stillness.label: Stillness

model.title: Compounding
model.body: Small consistent gains dominate large sporadic ones, and the effect is invisible until suddenly it is not. The counterintuitive part: nearly all the value arrives at the end.
model.action: Identify one habit that compounds. Protect it above anything urgent.
model.label: Mental Model

arabic.meaning: God willing, it will be good
arabic.use: Said when an outcome is uncertain. Graceful and appropriate almost anywhere.
arabic.label: Arabic

drill.title: Review Your Own Work Cold
drill.body: Leave it 24 hours, then review as if a stranger wrote it and you are looking for errors. You will find them. Reviewing immediately finds nothing.
drill.action: Re-open yesterday's work. Find three things to fix.
drill.label: Drill

health.title: Zone 5 Once A Week
health.body: Short maximal intervals raise VO2max faster than steady work. Four minutes hard, four easy, four times. Unpleasant, brief, and disproportionately effective.
health.action: One 4x4 interval session. Only if Zone 2 is already habitual.
health.label: Health

quote.name: Henry Ford
quote.quote: Whether you think you can, or you think you can't — you're right.

lesson.lesson: Gratitude is not only the greatest of virtues, but the parent of all others.

case.title: SpaceX: Reusable Rockets
case.story: Every expert said reusable rockets were impossible. SpaceX landed Falcon 9 first stage in 2015. Launch cost dropped from $150M to $28M. Changed the industry.
case.lesson: Impossible is a consensus opinion, not a fact. When everyone says something can't be done, check if they've done the math or just the tradition.

fpna.title: Scenario Planning
fpna.body: Always model 3: Base, Bull (+20%), Bear (–20%). Present the range. Executives hate surprises.

cfo.title: FC Interview: Top 5 Questions
cfo.body: 1. Walk me through month-end close. 2. How do you handle a material variance? 3. What internal controls have you implemented? 4. Describe your IFRS 16 experience. 5. How do you present bad news to management? Prepare 2-min answers for all five.

money_hack.title: SIP on Salary Day
money_hack.body: Set SIP date = salary day + 1. Invest before you spend. Pay yourself first.

dubai.title: Month-end close is the first question
dubai.body: Not 'walk me through your CV' — 'walk me through your close'. They want the day count, what runs on which day, where it breaks, and what you did about it.
dubai.targets: A close you shortened from 10 days to 6 is a better answer than any certificate.
dubai.action: Write your close calendar as a day-by-day list. Learn it.

desk.productivity: Define 'done' before starting. Vague tasks never finish.

father.title: Let her struggle briefly
father.do: When a toy is just out of reach, wait five seconds before helping.
father.why: Effort tolerance is trainable. Instant rescue is comfortable for you and teaches her that difficulty is someone else's problem.

father.title: Do one thing badly
father.do: Take over a task you normally leave to her mother, and accept doing it worse for a fortnight.
father.why: Competence gaps between parents are self-reinforcing — the more skilled parent does more, and the gap widens. Deliberately absorbing the early incompetence is how it closes.

life_wisdom.teaching: The Jain tradition values incremental letting-go over dramatic gestures — small consistent reduction beats one grand sacrifice.
life_wisdom.apply: Do not overhaul the budget in one heroic month. Cut one recurring thing permanently. Repeat next month. Sustainable beats spectacular.

life_wisdom.teaching: A practice of extending goodwill outward in rings — to yourself, someone loved, someone neutral, someone difficult.
life_wisdom.apply: The difficult person is the point of the exercise. Pick the colleague who frustrates you most and find one thing they are genuinely right about.

speaking.title: Shorten your sentences
speaking.drill: Take a written paragraph of your own and read it aloud, splitting every sentence longer than 15 words.
speaking.why: Your written voice is already short. Spoken sentences drift longer under pressure — this recalibrates it.

interview_tech.q: How would you use automation or AI in the finance function without losing control?
interview_tech.a: Automate the deterministic and keep judgement human. Good candidates: bank reconciliation matching, invoice coding, intercompany elimination, variance flagging, and first-draft commentary. Bad candidates: provisioning, impairment, anything requiring an assertion to auditors. The control question is auditability — if you cannot explain how the output was produced and reperform it, it is not usable in a statutory process. Keep a human approval step on anything that posts to the ledger.

interview_tech.q: Your auditor raises going concern. How do you respond?
interview_tech.a: Take it seriously and answer with evidence, not reassurance. Provide a cash flow forecast covering at least twelve months from signing, with the assumptions documented and stress cases run; the status of facilities including expiry dates and covenant projections; and board-approved mitigating actions with dates. If there is material uncertainty, the honest route is disclosure rather than argument — an unqualified opinion with a material uncertainty paragraph is survivable; a fight with the auditor that ends in a qualification is not.

interview_soft.q: How do you explain a complex financial concept to a non-finance audience?
interview_soft.a: Demonstrate it rather than describe it. Pick something like IFRS 16 or working capital and explain it in the answer, in plain words, in under 30 seconds, with a number. The technique: one analogy, one number, one consequence. Then stop. The most common failure is finance people proving they understand it instead of making the other person understand it.

interview_soft.q: Describe a time you led a team through significant change.
interview_soft.a: Use the ERP implementation — it is the strongest card in your hand. Cover what changed for the people, not just the systems: roles that disappeared, processes relearned, the period where everything took longer. Explain how you handled the dip in morale at go-live, who resisted and how you brought them round, and the measurable outcome. The 40% close reduction is the proof point; the retention of the team through it is the actual answer.
